read.sections.1.text.back: Real trade networks are much bigger. The Silk Road started being used more than 2,000 years ago. The Silk Road was not one road, but many land and sea routes, which connected China with Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe. Silk from China was carried west, while horses and glass were carried east. In the Indian Ocean, sailors made use of the monsoon winds, which change direction twice a year. Ships could sail out with one wind and come home with the next wind. Ports in East Africa, Arabia, India, Southeast Asia and China traded spices, cloth, gold and fine ceramics. In Africa, camels crossed the Sahara Desert carrying salt south and gold north. Timbuktu, in the Mali Empire, became rich thanks to this trade.
read.sections.1.text.source: Real trade networks were much bigger. The Silk Roads began more than 2,000 years ago. They were many land and sea routes, not one road, and they linked China with Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe. Silk from China travelled west, while horses and glass travelled east. On the Indian Ocean, sailors used the monsoon winds, which change direction twice a year. Ships could sail out on one wind and come home on the next. Ports in East Africa, Arabia, India, Southeast Asia and China traded spices, cloth, gold and fine pottery. In Africa, camels crossed the Sahara Desert, carrying salt south and gold north. Timbuktu, in the Mali Empire, grew rich from this trade.

read.sections.2.text.note: Sensitive: "bought and sold enslaved people" is "memperjualbelikan orang-orang yang diperbudak"; kept as short and factual as the English.
read.sections.2.text.back: Traders carried ideas, not only goods. Paper was first made in China, then the way to make paper spread along those routes to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe. Religions and languages also moved along with the traders. Timbuktu became famous for its books and teachers. In Riverstone, the potter's note shows an idea on the move, because a visiting trader shared a new way to decorate jars. But trade did not help everyone equally. Some traders became rich, while others lost money. On some routes, traders also bought and sold enslaved people, who were forced to work for others.

Religions and languages also travelled with traders. Timbuktu became famous for its books and teachers. In Riverstone, the potter's note shows an idea on the move, because a visiting trader shared a new way to decorate jars. But trade did not help everyone equally. Some traders grew rich, while others lost out. On some routes, traders also bought and sold enslaved people, who were forced to work for others.

watch.summary.note: Kept the video's English phrase "'world wide web'" (the video says it) and added "(internet)" so learners understand it.
watch.summary.back: This animated video tells the story of the Silk Road. It explains how, more than 2,000 years ago, trade started to grow between China and the lands to its west. The Silk Road was not one road. The Silk Road was a network of many routes that connected cities across Asia with the Middle East and Europe. Most traders did not make the whole journey. They carried goods on one part of the route, then handed them to another trader. Silk, spices, horses and many other goods moved along the route. Ideas moved too. Beliefs, languages, art and new ways of making things spread from one place to another. Some of these changes still affect how people live now. The video calls the Silk Road the 'world wide web' (internet) of the old days, because it connected so many people.
watch.summary.source: This animated video tells the story of the Silk Road. It explains how, more than 2,000 years ago, trade began to grow between China and lands to the west. The Silk Road was not one road. It was a network of many routes that linked towns across Asia to the Middle East and Europe. Most traders did not travel the whole way. They carried goods along one part, then passed them on to other traders. Silk, spices, horses and many other goods moved along the routes. Ideas moved too. Beliefs, languages, art and new ways of making things spread from place to place. Some of these changes still shape how people live today. The video calls the Silk Road an early 'world wide web', because it linked so many people.

read.sections.0.heading.source: Trade links places into a network

read.sections.0.text.back: Trading means giving goods to get other goods or money in return. Goods are things people make or grow, like tea, jars or cloth. In this fictional network, the hill village sends tea by cart to Riverstone. Boats carry that tea and clay jars from Riverstone down the river to Coastport. At this port, traders exchange them for cloth and salt from ships that stop there. No single trader makes the whole journey. Each person carries goods on only one part of the route. Together, these links form a network. If the river water is too shallow for boats, the traders have to find another way.
read.sections.0.text.source: Trade means giving goods to get other goods or money back. Goods are things people make or grow, like tea, jars or cloth. In the fictional network, the hill village sends tea by cart to Riverstone. Boats carry the tea and Riverstone's clay jars down the river to Coastport. At this port, traders swap them for cloth and salt from visiting ships. No single trader makes the whole journey. Each person carries the goods along one part of the route. Together, these links form a network. If the river is too low for boats, traders must find another way.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: Trading means giving something to get something. Goods are things people make or grow. Carts carry tea from the hill village to Riverstone. Boats carry tea and jars to Coastport. At the port, people exchange that tea and those jars for cloth and salt. No one person makes the whole journey. Each person carries goods on one part of the route. All these links form a network. If the river is shallow, traders need another way.

If the river is low, traders need a new way.

write.example.back: First, the jar was made by a potter in Riverstone. Next, a boat trader carried it down the river to Coastport, together with tea from the hill village. These places are connected by the cart road, the river and the sea. At the port, a trader exchanged the jar and tea for cloth and salt. An idea could move when a sailor saw the pattern on the jar and then copied it at home. This shows that trade can move ideas, not only goods.
write.example.source: First, the jar is made by a potter in Riverstone. Next, a boat trader carries it down the river to Coastport, with tea from the hill village. The places are linked by a cart road, a river and the sea. At the port, a trader swaps the jar and the tea for cloth and salt. An idea could travel when a sailor sees the pattern on the jar and copies it at home. This shows that trade can move ideas as well as goods.
